positions.commentary: The speaker mentions that Tesla is considered a contentious stock where analysts are unlikely to come out and say it is overrated or a sell due to career risk.

thesis: This episode argues that Tesla is a contentious stock where analysts face career risk if they publicly recommend a sell, and it highlights a specific instance where a former bullish analyst's valuation was criticized by the New York Times.

claims.claim: The speaker notes that Adam Jonas was very bullish on Tesla years ago, but the New York Times published an article criticizing his recommendation, suggesting the valuation made no sense and it wouldn't work.
claims.quote: there's an article in the New York Times that was kind of poo-poohing Adam Jonas's Tesla recommendation several years back when he was very bullish on it. And they're like, oh, it doesn't make any sense. The valuation doesn't make any sense. It's not going to work.

claims.claim: The speaker mentions that Tesla is considered a contentious stock where analysts are unlikely to come out and say it is overrated or a sell due to career risk.
claims.quote: especially if you're thinking about a contentious stock like Tesla or Navidia today, I can't imagine an analyst wanting to come out today and say, oh, Navidia is super overrated.
